subject.title: [Feature]: Collapsible messages in Control UI chat

question: Should Control UI add inline collapse for long assistant Markdown, and what default threshold, newest-message behavior, and global expand/collapse policy should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful but it is a new UX policy, and current main already has overlapping side-reader, tool-message, JSON, and duplicate-message disclosure paths that should remain coherent.

options.title: Approve Bounded Inline Collapse
options.body: Implement a small first version that collapses older long assistant messages by line or height threshold, keeps the latest active response readable, and defers global controls unless maintainers want them now.

options.title: Use Side Reader Only
options.body: Decline inline collapse for now and treat the existing canvas/side-reader flow as the supported long-message escape hatch.

options.title: Defer To Broader Chat UX
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader chat readability and accessibility design decides all disclosure states together.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Inline Collapse
recommendation.body: Implement a small first version that collapses older long assistant messages by line or height threshold, keeps the latest active response readable, and defers global controls unless maintainers want them now.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/UX decision in an area where recent chat scannability and disclosure work makes steipete the best routing candidate from the available history.
